question.value: Compare stellar and dust structures in cluster-lensed SMGs and investigate their evolutionary connection to compact quiescent galaxies.

evidence.quote: we present the observations and analyses of the stellar and dust components in cluster-lensed SMGs at both integrated and spatially resolved scales.
Our observations are consistent with the hypothesis that SMGs are progenitors of the compact quiescent galaxies at slightly lower redshift.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2015.1.01548, #2016.1.00372 and #2017.1.01658.S.
We present an ALMA 1.3 mm (Band 6) continuum survey

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: 15 continuum-only targets: 233 GHz (1.287 mm); 5 targets: continuum and at least one CO line; effective continuum frequencies 224–238 GHz

evidence.quote: For 15 sources without previous spectroscopic redshift determination, we performed continuum-only observations with a central frequency at 233 GHz (corresponding to 1.287 mm).

referee_caveats_inferred: The 26 fitted components include multiple images and HLS1314 clumps; independence and repeated-source weighting need explicit treatment in correlation errors.
Both axes of the main structural correlation contain the fitted dust radius; reproducing the stated mock-data test is essential.
The largest dust source is also the one exceeding its recoverable angular scale.
A cross-sectional comparison with stacked evolutionary tracks does not establish individual galaxies' histories.
No differential magnification is assumed although size ratios and stellar/dust tracers differ spatially.
HLS0600 has inconsistent redshifts in the text and physical-properties table; the HLS0011/HLS0111 naming also needs reconciliation.
The first two project identifiers are printed without an .S suffix; archive lookup requires resolving those literal identifiers.
